regulations.title: Medical electrical equipment - Part 1: General requirements for basic safety and essential performance
Medical electrical equipment - Part 1: General requirements for basic safety and essential performance (European version)
Audio, video and similar electronic apparatus - Safety requirements
Mechanical safety of cathode ray tubes

tests.requirement: MOBILE ME EQUIPMENT with SAFE WORKING LOAD on horizontal plane with locking device activated and castors in worst case position - further movement no more than 50 mm when force of 15% of weight (but less than 150 N) applied in different directions except upward, at highest point or 1.5 m from floor

Grips and other handling devices - ME EQUIPMENT other than PORTABLE EQUIPMENT with mass over 20 kg requiring lifting provided with suitable handling means or ACCOMPANYING DOCUMENTS specify safe lifting method
tests.result: Portable equipment and less than 20 kg

tests.requirement: Handles suitably placed to enable ME EQUIPMENT or its part to be carried by two or more persons
PORTABLE ME EQUIPMENT with mass > 20 kg provided with one or more carrying-handles suitably placed to enable carrying by two or more persons as confirmed by actual carrying
Carrying handles and grips and their means of attachment withstood loading test
Suitability of means of protecting against unacceptable RISK of expelled parts determined by assessment and examination of RISK MANAGEMENT FILE
Cathode ray tube(s) complied with IEC 60065:2001 Clause 18 or IEC 61965
Acoustic energy (including infra- and ultrasound) and vibration

Human exposure to acoustic energy and vibration from ME EQUIPMENT doesn't result in unacceptable RISK based on tests of 9.6.2 and 9.6.3, confirmed in RISK MANAGEMENT FILE including audibility of auditory alarm signals and PATIENT sensitivity
Acoustic energy
PATIENT, OPERATOR, and other persons not exposed to acoustic energy from ME EQUIPMENT in NORMAL USE except for auditory ALARM SIGNALS - 80 dBA for cumulative exposure of 24 h over 24 h period
tests.result: The noises of Infrared No-Touch Forehead Thermometer on the back side and upper is 51.3 dBA

tests.requirement: 83 dBA (when halving the cumulative exposure time)
140 dBC (peak) sound pressure level for impulsive or impact acoustic energy
RISK MANAGEMENT FILE examined for RISKS associated with infrasound or ultrasound addressed in RISK MANAGEMENT PROCESS

Hand-transmitted vibration - means provided to protect PATIENT and OPERATOR when hand-transmitted frequency-weighted r.m.s. acceleration in NORMAL USE exceeds 2.5 m/s2 for cumulative time of 8 h during 24 h period
Accelerations for different times, inversely proportional to square root of time
Requirements applied to vessels and parts of ME EQUIPMENT subject to pressure resulting in rupture and unacceptable RISK
Pneumatic and hydraulic parts of ME EQUIPMENT or ACCESSORIES met requirements based on examination of RISK MANAGEMENT FILE - no unacceptable RISK from loss of pressure or vacuum
No unacceptable RISK from fluid jet caused by leakage or component failure
Elements especially pipes and hoses leading to unacceptable RISK protected against harmful external effects
Reservoirs and similar vessels leading to unacceptable RISK are automatically depressurized when ME EQUIPMENT is isolated from power supply

semantic_fragments.content: For MOBILE ME EQUIPMENT: further movement (after initial elastic movement) shall be no more than 50 mm when a force of 15% of weight of unit (but less than 150 N) is applied in different directions, except a direction with an upwards component, at highest point of ME EQUIPMENT but 1.5 m from floor. Test performed with SAFE WORKING LOAD, placed on horizontal plane with locking device activated and castors in worst case position.

PATIENT, OPERATOR, and other persons are not to be exposed to acoustic energy from ME EQUIPMENT in NORMAL USE except for auditory ALARM SIGNALS exceeding: 80 dBA for a cumulative exposure of 24 h over a 24 h period; 83 dBA when halving the cumulative exposure time; 140 dBC (peak) sound pressure level for impulsive or impact acoustic energy. The Infrared No-Touch Forehead Thermometer measured 51.3 dBA at the back side and upper, which is within the 80 dBA limit.

Hand-transmitted vibration protection required for PATIENT and OPERATOR when hand-transmitted frequency-weighted r.m.s. acceleration generated in NORMAL USE exceeds: 2.5 m/s2 for a cumulative time of 8 h during a 24 h period; accelerations for different times are inversely proportional to square root of time. Measured at points of hand contact with PATIENT or OPERATOR, except for INTENDED USE vibrations.
